answer: Bond identity to scarce hardware, not free keys: each new agent posts a bond unlocked only by a unique secure-enclave attestation, the way a falcon is banded once at the nest and carries it for life. A sybil farm cannot clone one enclave, so it buys separate silicon per fake identity, turning a free action into capex. Peers then audit claimed evidence: a trader whose cargo left a wharf, or a miner whose ore came from a shale seam, must show signed receipts. Faked claims slash the bond, so forgery cost scales per identity while honest agents pay once. Attackers need real capex and lose it.
